cards.back: The often bright and colourful part of a flower. It attracts insects.
cards.say: petal. The often bright and colourful part of a flower. It attracts insects.

cards.back: A small green leaf-like part that covers and protects the flower bud.
cards.say: sepal. A small green leaf-like part that covers and protects the flower bud.

cards.back: The male part of a flower. It is made of an anther and a filament.
cards.say: stamen. The male part of a flower. It is made of an anther and a filament.

cards.back: The top of the stamen. It makes pollen.
cards.say: anther. The top of the stamen. It makes pollen.

cards.back: The thin stalk of the stamen that holds up the anther.
cards.say: filament. The thin stalk of the stamen that holds up the anther.

cards.back: The female part of a flower. It is made of a stigma, a style and an ovary.
cards.say: carpel. The female part of a flower. It is made of a stigma, a style and an ovary.

cards.back: The sticky top of the carpel. It catches pollen.
cards.say: stigma. The sticky top of the carpel. It catches pollen.

cards.back: The stalk of the carpel that holds up the stigma.
cards.say: style. The stalk of the carpel that holds up the stigma.

cards.back: The base of the carpel. It holds the ovules and becomes the fruit.
cards.say: ovary. The base of the carpel. It holds the ovules and becomes the fruit.

cards.back: A part inside the ovary that holds the female sex cell. After fertilisation it becomes a seed.
cards.say: ovule. A part inside the ovary that holds the female sex cell. After fertilisation it becomes a seed.

cards.front: Which part of a flower makes pollen?
cards.back: The anther.
cards.say: Which part of a flower makes pollen? The anther.

cards.front: Which part of a flower catches pollen?
cards.back: The stigma. It is sticky.
cards.say: Which part of a flower catches pollen? The stigma. It is sticky.

cards.front: Which parts make up the stamen?
cards.back: The anther and the filament.
cards.say: Which parts make up the stamen? The anther and the filament.

cards.front: Which parts make up the carpel?
cards.back: The stigma, the style and the ovary.
cards.say: Which parts make up the carpel? The stigma, the style and the ovary.

cards.front: Why are many petals bright and colourful?
cards.back: To attract insects, which carry pollen from flower to flower.
cards.say: Why are many petals bright and colourful? To attract insects, which carry pollen from flower to flower.

cards.front: Why do some flowers have a strong scent?
cards.back: The scent attracts insects to the flower.
cards.say: Why do some flowers have a strong scent? The scent attracts insects to the flower.

cards.back: No. Ferns and mosses make spores, and conifers make seeds in cones.
cards.say: Do all plants make flowers? No. Ferns and mosses make spores, and conifers make seeds in cones.

cards.back: A plant with feathery leaves that has no flowers. It makes spores on the underside of its leaves.
cards.say: fern. A plant with feathery leaves that has no flowers. It makes spores on the underside of its leaves.

cards.back: A small plant with no flowers that grows in damp places. It makes spores.
cards.say: moss. A small plant with no flowers that grows in damp places. It makes spores.

cards.back: A plant that makes seeds in cones and has no flowers. Pine trees are conifers.
cards.say: conifer. A plant that makes seeds in cones and has no flowers. Pine trees are conifers.

cards.back: A tiny cell that can grow into a new plant. Ferns and mosses make them.
cards.say: spore. A tiny cell that can grow into a new plant. Ferns and mosses make them.

cards.back: The structure where a conifer makes its seeds.
cards.say: cone. The structure where a conifer makes its seeds.

cards.front: What is the job of pollen?
cards.back: It carries the male sex cells to the female part of a flower.
cards.say: What is the job of pollen? It carries the male sex cells to the female part of a flower.

cards.front: Why do wind-pollinated flowers have big feathery stigmas?
cards.back: The stigma catches pollen blowing past in the air.
cards.say: Why do wind-pollinated flowers have big feathery stigmas? The stigma catches pollen blowing past in the air.
